rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L45 Debrief bolds a 10-word clause '**and the first root instructions file in this directory.**' (one bold on slide, but over the handle cap; see suggestion). L74 '**A daily agent, scheduled, with a week of observation behind it.**' is a whole lead sentence, but curriculum/module-shape.md L42-43 prescribes 'Bring to Module [N]: Bold the ask', so the template mandates the spend. L12-15 LO verbs are template-mandated. Harm (emphasis dilution) absent: one bold per slide.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L61 declarative 'The model will change under this' lands as a declaration at the module's generalising moment; module-file headings are labels/orientation (Start here, Debrief, Next), not exercise/lecture headings; L55 'Fix the output, then fix the rule' is an imperative. No label standing in for a required claim.

(class c kicker risk) adds the named practice the header and quote do not state; L63 'The model will change. L87 `## Next` runs four sentences against the 'two plain sentences' closer rule, but it is the carry-in task, not a mechanism aside or coined term; filed as suggestion, not gate (red thread L91 asks align-not-add).

suggestions.now: Five minutes. A retro, **and the first root instructions file in this directory.** The agent writes the rules every agent here reads: what worked, what rubbed, what got repeated.
suggestions.proposed: Five minutes. A retro, and the **first root instructions file** in this directory. The agent writes the rules every agent here reads: what worked, what rubbed, what got repeated.

suggestions.now: Before the next module, have the agent build a few more agents you need. Pick by pain: a task you keep doing manually. Meeting prep and calendar triage are fine starters. Keep the first version proposal-only: the agent drafts, ranks, or prepares; you decide what leaves the system.
